expectations.text: The hook handles form state and validation only — no network calls, no rendering, no side effects beyond state
expectations.evidence: Hook manages values/errors/touched/isSubmitting. No fetch, no DOM refs, no useEffect. onSubmit callback is caller-provided.

expectations.text: The hook has a descriptive name starting with 'use' that makes its purpose clear (e.g. useLoginForm, not useForm)
expectations.evidence: Named useLoginForm — specific to the login domain

expectations.text: Both email and password fields have validation with clear rules (email format, password length/requirements)
expectations.evidence: validateEmail checks required + regex pattern; validatePassword checks required + min 8 chars

expectations.text: The hook returns a clear, usable object with values, errors, and handler functions
expectations.evidence: Returns { values, errors, touched, isSubmitting, handleChange, handleBlur, handleSubmit, resetForm }

expectations.text: Validation errors are shown in a UX-aware way — errors don't appear before the user has interacted (touched state or similar)
expectations.evidence: touched state tracked; handleBlur marks fields touched; errors only validated on blur and on subsequent changes
